messages.content: You are a precise information extraction system. You only output valid JSON.

Find all event triggers of the event types below in the document.

Event types:
- Attack: An agent physically assaults or launches a violent attack on a target (bombing, ambush, raid, shooting, assault). (e.g. attack, assaulted, ambushed, bombing)
- Military_operation: Organised armed conflict between forces: a war, battle, campaign, siege or military operation as a whole. (e.g. war, battle, fought, campaign)
- Conquering: An agent takes control of a place or group by force (capture, seize, conquer, occupy). (e.g. captured, conquer, seized, taken)
- Killing: A killer causes the death of a victim (an agent is responsible for the death). (e.g. killed, killing, murdered, massacre)
- Death: Someone dies, with focus on the death itself rather than on a killer. (e.g. died, death, dead, deaths)
- Bodily_harm: Someone is physically injured or wounded. (e.g. injured, wounded, injuries, hurt)
- Catastrophe: A natural or man-made disaster happens (storm, flood, earthquake, crash, fire, accident). (e.g. hurricane, storm, flood, earthquake)
- Destroying: Something is destroyed completely (destroyed, demolished, sunk, burned down). (e.g. destroyed, destruction, demolished, sank)
- Damaging: Something is damaged but not completely destroyed. (e.g. damage, damaged, struck, battered)
- Statement: A speaker communicates a message (says, states, announces, describes, reports). (e.g. said, stated, announced, described)
- Change_of_leadership: Leadership or control of a polity or organisation changes (election, coup, revolution, ousting, independence, replacement of a leader). (e.g. elected, coup, revolution, ousted)
- Arriving: An agent arrives at or reaches a place. (e.g. arrived, reached, entered, landed)

Trigger annotation rules:
- A trigger is the single word (sometimes a short phrase) that most clearly expresses the event; it can be a verb ("attacked") or a noun ("attack", "war", "fires").
- Annotate EVERY occurrence: if the same event is mentioned several times ("the fires ... the fires ..."), list each occurrence as a separate entry.
- Only annotate the 12 event types below; ignore other kinds of events.
- Disambiguation:
  * Military_operation = a war, battle, campaign or siege as a whole; Attack = one specific assault, bombing, raid, shelling or ambush.
  * Conquering = capturing or taking control of a place or group (captured, seized, took, defeated and occupied).
  * Killing = someone or something kills (killed, massacre, slain, executed); Death = the dying itself (died, death, dead, fatalities).
  * Catastrophe = the disaster event itself (storm, hurricane, fire, flood, crash, accident); Destroying = something is completely destroyed; Damaging = something is damaged but not destroyed.
  * Bodily_harm = injury or wounding (injured, wounded, injuries).

Return JSON: {"triggers": [{"trigger": "<word copied from the document>", "type": "<event type>"}]}
List one entry per occurrence, in reading order. Return {"triggers": []} if there is none.

### Example 1
Document:
lion air flight 904 was a scheduled domestic passenger flight from husein unk international airport in bandung to ngurah rai international airport in bali, indonesia. On 13 April 2013, the Boeing 737-800 operating the flight crashed into water short of runway while on final approach to land. All 101 passengers and 7 crew on board survived the accident. at 15:10 local time (07:10 utc), the aircraft crashed approximately short of the seawall protecting the threshold of runway 09. The aircraft's fuselage broke into two and 46 people were injured, 4 of them seriously. Among the findings contained in the final investigation report was that the crew continued the approach in adverse weather conditions beyond the point at which the approved procedure would have required to abort the landing. The subsequent attempt to go around was made too late to avoid the impact with the sea. It was also determined that there were no issues with the aircraft and all systems were operating normally.
Output:
{"triggers": [{"trigger": "crashed", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "approach", "type": "Arriving"}, {"trigger": "crashed", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "broke", "type": "Destroying"}, {"trigger": "injured", "type": "Bodily_harm"}, {"trigger": "approach", "type": "Arriving"}]}

### Example 2
Document:
Airblue Flight 202 was a scheduled Airblue domestic passenger flight from Karachi's Jinnah International Airport to Islamabad's Benazir Bhutto International Airport. On 28 July 2010, the Airbus A321-231 narrow-body jet airliner serving the flight crashed near Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan, killing all 146 passengers and six crew on board. It is the deadliest air accident to occur in Pakistan to date. The aircraft crashed in the Margalla Hills north of Islamabad after air traffic controllers lost contact with the flight crew during their attempt to land in dense fog and heavy monsoon rain. The accident was the first fatal crash involving an Airbus A321, a long variant of the Airbus A320 family of short to medium range airliners. Based in Islamabad, Airblue is Pakistan's second largest airline, with over 30% share of the domestic market. At the time of the accident the airline operated seven aircraft, all in the A320 family.
Output:
{"triggers": [{"trigger": "crashed", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "killing", "type": "Killing"}, {"trigger": "accident", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "crashed", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "accident", "type": "Catastrophe"}, {"trigger": "crash", "type": "Catastrophe"}]}

### Example 3
Document:
Palair Macedonian Airlines Flight 301 was a scheduled international passenger flight from Switzerland's Zurich-Kloten Airport to International Airport Skopje, Skopje, which crashed shortly after take off on March 5, 1993. The Fokker 100 was operated by Palair Macedonian Airlines, the national airline of Macedonia. A total of 83 people, 79 passengers and 4 crew members, were killed in the crash while 14 people survived. at the time, it was the deadliest plane crash in macedonia. It was surpassed a few months later on the same year when a Yakovlev Yak-42 slammed onto a mountain near Ohrid. It was the deadliest aviation accident involving a Fokker 100 at the time it took place, a record it maintained until TAM Flight 402 crashed on 31 October 1996. Flight 301 is still the second-deadliest Fokker 100 crash. The investigation of the disaster, which was assisted by the Dutch investigation team, concluded that the cause of the accident was due to the accumulation of ice on the wings of the aircraft. Also known as atmospheric icing, the ice accumulation caused the deterioration of lift force. Failure to adhere to the correct procedure for handling an atmospheric icing was also cited as one of the causes of the crash.
Output:
{"triggers": [{"trigger": "crashed", "type": "Damaging"}, {"trigger": "killed", "type": "Killing"}, {"trigger": "crashed", "type": "Damaging"}]}
